next_action.rationale: All 186 stuck orders carry the split-reservation exception flag. Auditing allocation exceptions for east-node orders since 06:00 will determine: (1) is split-reservation a new behavior in v18 or pre-existing, (2) do all split-reservation exceptions hold orders or only these 186, (3) what stock condition triggers the flag. This is the highest-confidence discriminator: if split-reservation is new in v18 and correlates with stock issues only after v18, then H1 is likely; if the flag is pre-existing and all such orders normally clear pickup, then something downstream (H2/H3) is different.
next_action.expected_information_gain: Clarify whether v18 is creating split-reservation flagging incorrectly, and whether split-reservation is intended to block pickup or is a secondary defect

next_action.rationale: H1 is now inferred with discriminating evidence: 100% of held orders are v18-routed with split-reservation flag, and 0% of held orders are outside that cohort. Other nodes are unaffected. This perfectly discriminates v18 from carrier-wide or dock-capacity causes. The remaining unknown is whether v18's split-reservation hold is intended behavior or a defect. Reviewing rule history will show: (1) what split-reservation was designed to do, (2) whether v18 introduced or changed this behavior, (3) whether hold-until-resolution is documented. This determines if v18 is functioning as designed (not a defect, needs operational mitigation) or contains a bug (defect mitigation required).
next_action.expected_information_gain: Clarify whether split-reservation hold is intended design or a bug in v18, narrowing the mitigation path

next_action.rationale: ROOT1 is established with discriminating evidence: v18 triggered split-reservation for 100% of held orders and 0% outside that cohort; other nodes unaffected rules out carrier-wide or dock issues; v18 technically sound per validation but validation gap exists in carrier scheduling. Reverting v18's east-node-first reservation priority will: (1) restore orders to previous allocation logic, (2) immediately clear the split-reservation exception flag, (3) re-enable carrier pickup progression for the 186 stuck orders. This is reversible, idempotent, and scoped to v18's east-node priority change only. The reversion is the fastest path to restore order flow; investigation into the carrier scheduling gap can continue post-mitigation

next_action.rationale: H3_REFINED is now disproven (dock capacity is normal). All east-node orders are stuck regardless of allocation rule (m8_r_revert), but the dock has space (m8_r_dock), meaning orders never reached dock staging. This narrows root cause to: (1) carrier system rejection/blocking of east-node requests, (2) allocation-to-carrier handoff failure, or (3) inventory issue. next_action.rationale: Root cause is now fully established and understood: carrier confirmation lag (47min median) exceeds slot validity (30min), causing EXC-0921 orders to expire their pickup slots before confirmation. This is a pre-existing carrier integration timing issue, not a defect in v18 or current operations. Mitigation is slot correction to refresh/extend slots for the affected orders (east-node overnight cohort), followed by replay of held allocations. Authority exists for reversible slot correction with Carrier Ops approval. The incident is understood and ready for targeted recovery action. Gate decision: PROCEED with slot correction to correct feed and replay.
